requirements.evidence: CreateQueue trims/validates and slugifies with entity-scoped duplicate detection plus race handling (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:20-48); UpdateQueue supports the named nullable name/slug/isActive parameters and tolerates the queue's own slug (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:15-59); SetQueueAccess upserts, revokes and audits with the cross-entity check (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:22-47, 78-85); QueuePolicy implements create/update/manageAccess/call and both call paths enforce it in the required order (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:17-64, app/Models/Ticket.php:95-105, app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32). Gap: isUniqueViolation treats any SQLSTATE 23000 as a duplicate slug (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:66-76, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:87-97).

conventions.evidence: Domain writes are one Action per use case authorizing internally (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:18, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:22, app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:22); authorization lives in an auto-discovered policy (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php); generated-style migration with constrained cascade FKs and a reversible down() (database/migrations/2026_10_29_071113_create_queue_access_table.php:14-29); deliberate #[Fillable] on the new model (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:11); docs and CHANGELOG kept in sync (docs/business-rules.md:1, docs/database-schema.md:5, CHANGELOG.md:21); Pest tests ship with the change.

security.evidence: Every write authorizes before mutating data (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:18, app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:22, app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:22) and both call paths authorize (app/Models/Ticket.php:101, app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32); the policy denies non-members, cross-entity members and corrupted non-array grants (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:41-67); all input is validated (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:23-29, app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:56-70); mass assignment is limited to #[Fillable] plus an explicit attribute whitelist (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:24-36); no UI or output escaping surface in scope.

tests.evidence: New Pest suites cover create/update/access/policy and both call paths, including unauthorized and other-entity cases (tests/Feature/Queue/CreateQueueTest.php:113-127, tests/Feature/Queue/UpdateQueueTest.php:128-149, tests/Feature/Queue/SetQueueAccessTest.php:141-177), the DB unique race (tests/Feature/Queue/CreateQueueTest.php:61-87), audit on grant/revoke plus the silent empty revoke (tests/Feature/Queue/SetQueueAccessTest.php:91-103), corrupted permission values (tests/Feature/Queue/QueuePolicyTest.php:109-120) and denial in every call mode (tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php:255-303); only gap is the update-slug race path.

simplicity.evidence: Task-critical code is lean and reuses the existing Queue/Ticket actions, but database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:60-117 overrides Factory::for() and re-aligns entity_id via afterMaking/forceFill although the contract only needs a same-entity default, and the slugExists/duplicateSlug/isUniqueViolation trio is duplicated between app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:51-76 and app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:71-97.

readability.evidence: Actions and policy read clearly (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:20-48, app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:41-64); the factory's shared-by-reference &$entity closures and two alignment helpers take effort to follow (database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:23-117), and the manual JSON re-decode in app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:53-64 is subtle.

scope.evidence: All changed files serve the task (three actions, policy, model, factory, migration, three docs, tests); the factory's bidirectional entity alignment and its dedicated tests (tests/Feature/Queue/QueueAccessTest.php:45-61) go beyond the stated factory contract.

issues.explanation: The policy imports App\Models\UserRole while the project's enums live in App\Enums (see app/Enums/QueuePermission.php:5-8 and App\Enums\TicketStatus); if no UserRole enum exists under App\Models this is a fatal class-not-found for every ability, so the namespace should be confirmed (it could not be verified from the diff).

isUniqueViolation (also app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:87-97) maps any SQLSTATE 23000 integrity error, including FK or NOT NULL violations from a concurrent delete, to a duplicate-slug ValidationException instead of only the (entity_id, slug) unique violation.

Overriding Factory::for() and silently rewriting entity_id on pinned memberships/queues (lines 94-116) is far heavier than the contract requires and can mutate existing factory data in surprising ways.
slugExists, duplicateSlug and isUniqueViolation are copy-pasted into app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:71-97; one shared helper or trait would keep the two actions from drifting apart.
The update path's DB unique race is untested (only tests/Feature/Queue/CreateQueueTest.php:61-87 covers a race), and SetQueueAccess has no test for a keyed (non-list) permissions array.
The is_string/json_decode branch only fires for corrupted scalar rows, which is hard to infer; a one-line comment would clarify why the array cast can still yield a string.

review.summary: The change implements queue creation/update without hard delete, the queue_access table/model/factory, audit-logged access grants, and a single QueuePolicy enforced by both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call(), with extensive Pest coverage and synced docs. It is close to mergeable; the remaining concerns are a suspicious App\Models\UserRole import, an over-engineered QueueAccessFactory alignment mechanism, duplicated slug-validation helpers and a couple of small test/edge-case gaps.
